objective: Replace the undersized degree-4 factor base with a target-independent divisor kernel and test a scalar-blind degree-15 solve.

public_discovery.sizing_reason: m times dimension must be at least n; dimension 8 is the smallest available divisor dimension above 15/2
public_discovery.candidate_source: all degree-8 divisors of T^15-1 over F2
public_discovery.admission: the factor-base cofactor classes can sum to zero with exactly two summands
public_discovery.selection_rule: among admitted candidates, maximize rational factor-base points; then minimize projected signed-Frobenius columns; then choose lexicographically lower divisor indices
allowed_inputs: rational points above each linearised kernel
cofactor-projected point equality up to signed Frobenius

column_reduction: Merge only cofactor projections that are equal up to signed Frobenius by public point arithmetic; never compute their discrete logs.
metrics: discovery wall, core-seconds and peak RSS
index-calculus wall, core-seconds, peak RSS, relations, trials, conflicts and linear algebra
rho wall, core-seconds, peak RSS, iterations and operation ledger
claim_boundary: One degree-15 completion is a larger toy result and does not establish a scaling law, crossover, novelty or SOTA.
